title: Polynomial-index weakly symplectic or unitary lattice bases for integral-trace skew-Hermitian forms over Albert type I or II division algebras
source_title: Lattices with skew-Hermitian forms over division algebras and unlikely intersections
author: Christopher Daw; Martin Orr
difficulty_reason: The quoted class-index version of Minkowski does not provide a basis compatible with the skew-Hermitian form while keeping polynomial discriminant bounds. The authors extract small nondegenerate rank-one or rank-two modules, control the complementary lattice and repeat the construction through distinct field and quaternion cases with explicit index and pairing-size estimates. They also bound the failure of involution-stability of the stabilizer order to remove the extra induction parameter, a nonroutine quantitative arithmetic construction before the later formal applications.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.2: D a totally real field or nonsplit totally indefinite quaternion division algebra over a totally real field, positive involution, nondegenerate skew-Hermitian form on a left D-vector space and full Z-lattice with integral reduced-trace pairing. Stabilizer order R=Stab_D(L); basis lies in L, has weakly symplectic/weakly unitary pairing pattern and polynomial bounds on index and pairing sizes in absolute discriminants. Constants depend only on rank m and Q-dimension of D; no polynomial dependence uniformly in varying m is claimed. Read exact3–4 and every new proof10–39: division-norm estimates, order conductor/antisymmetric element2.12, trace/discriminant calculations, adapted real D-norm, initial rank-one/two blocks4.4 and all three full inductive cases4.5 plus4.6. Classical Albert classification, real split symplectic-module linear algebra, Minkowski and prior DO22 discriminant identity are referenced foundations. No Zilber-Pink or Galois-orbit conclusion selected. Standard real split-basis lemma3.5 physical24 has a literal sign in its polarization sentence inconsistent with the preceding skew-Hermitian definition: that definition gives psi(x,y)-transpose in the mixed diagonal term; preserve both and the complete explicit subsequent normalization/direct-sum construction. This is bounded standard linear algebra notation, not an omitted new arithmetic denominator or induction core. Matrix Ma in3.6 is printed integral for arbitrary rational a though used as rational; source formula is retained. No sharp constants from Table1 separately claimed. Original PDF authors Christopher Daw/Martin Orr and10/2023/240 verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author combines noncommutative Minkowski selection, an antisymmetric quaternion element controlling dual-order denominators, and a rank-one or rank-two Gram-Schmidt induction with discriminant bounds. The quantitative arithmetic reduction of skew-Hermitian lattices is substantially beyond qualifying-exam algebra or geometry of numbers.
